title: Linear-size autocatalytic sets are asymptotically absent in the sparse binary polymer model
summary: In the sparse binary polymer model with reversible ligation and cleavage, we prove that for every fixed food horizon, fixed nonnegative catalysis intensity and fixed linear reaction budget, the probability of a nonempty reflexively autocatalytic and food-generated set within that budget tends to zero, at rate O(1/n). The probability that a single molecule catalyses a self-constructing reaction set also vanishes, cleavage included.
